statement: The low-tax test of the CFC rule is a comparison with half of the statutory rate (25% x 50% = 12.5%). statement: Condition (c) of s13(9), the Comptroller's satisfaction that the exemption is beneficial, is read as met whenever conditions (a) and (b) are met, because an exemption of a dividend can only reduce the resident's tax. The rule tests (a) as payer_income_taxed and (b) as payer_tax_rate not less than 15%.

statement: The same reading as D-sg-1 for individuals under s13(7A)(b): the exemption of foreign-sourced income received by a resident individual is treated as applying without a predicate on the Comptroller's satisfaction. statement: The 19% rate applies to the part of annual income up to JPY 8,000,000 of a company whose capital is JPY 100 million or less, and the standard rate to the rest: a marginal schedule. statement: Domestic dividends are excluded from income in full for shares above one third (affiliated-company and wholly owned shares), at 50% for shares above 5% and up to one third, and at 20% for shares of 5% or less. The 50% and 20% figures are used with the effect exclude because the law states the excluded portion.

statement: The CFC rule is modelled as full inclusion under 66-6(1) with the exemptions of 66-6(5): a specified foreign related company is exempt at a tax burden of 27% or more, any other foreign related company at 20% or more or when it passes the economic activity test (predicate cfc_activity). The partial inclusion of passive income under 66-6(6) is not modelled.

statement: The reconstruction surtax is 2.1% of the withholding tax, so the effective statutory rate is 20.42% (15.315% for listed shares). The rule layer composes it with the effect surtax before treaty caps, because a treaty cap limits the total tax charged. The surtax runs to 2037 under the Act; that end date is not a parameter and is not applied.

statement: Under the foreign subsidiary dividend exclusion 95% of the dividend is excluded; the Order fixes the deemed expense at 5% of the dividend. The parameter jp.inbound.exemption_expense_share (5) is therefore the included share, used with the effect share.

statement: Beneficial-owner safe harbours of STA 2018 No. 9 are modelled as conditional rules: item 4(1)-(3) (government, listed company, individual of the treaty partner) and item 3 (a 100% parent that itself qualifies as beneficial owner, holds the ratio for the 12 months of item 5, and is a 'qualifying person' with a treaty benefit not worse than the payee's). Not modelled: item 4(4) (payee held 100% by persons of items (1)-(3) with intermediate holders resident in China or the partner) and the condition of item 3(2) that every intermediate holder in a multi-tier chain qualifies; such a payee falls back to the factor analysis pred(bo). The pass-on factor of item 2(1) is exposed as a factor variable (passes_on_within_12m), not as a condition, because the announcement lists it as a factor to weigh, not a test.

statement: Share transfers are modelled in the restructure slot: a non-resident's direct transfer at 10% on consideration less cost; an indirect transfer only when the predicate indirect_transfer_purpose is no (re-characterisation under STA 2015 No. 7 item 1); the item 6 group safe harbour with its 80% relation and the property-rich 50% switch, item 6(3) (consideration entirely in shares) as the structure variable consideration_in_shares, item 6(2) (no reduction of the Chinese tax on a later indirect transfer) as the structure variable future_cn_tax_not_reduced, which the optimization layer derives by comparing the Chinese tax on a direct transfer by the transferee with that by the transferor; treaty Article 13 exemptions by holding_pct at the time of transfer, whereas the treaties say 'at any time in the twelve months before' (the caller passes the maximum of that period); the consideration defaults to net assets (STA 2014 No. 67 arts. 12, 14) unless an appraisal exists, which is an input not a rule. Stamp tax: both parties at 0.05%.

statement: A foreign company's gain on Thai shares is assessable income under s40(4)(ช) taxed by 15% withholding under s70 (rate schedule (2)(ข)); the base is the excess of price over cost, which the payer must determine. A non-resident individual is withheld at 15% (s50(2)(ก)); a resident individual's gain is s40(4)(ช) assessable income taxed with the year's other net income at the s48(1) schedule (effect schedule, the same table as dividends; expense deductions and the s47 bis credit are not modelled). Stamp duty 0.1% on the higher of paid-up value and price, paid by the transferor.

statement: The s13(8) 'subject to tax' condition is tested in the jurisdiction from which the dividend is received by Singapore, not up the chain: IRAS (e-Tax Guide on foreign-sourced income, para 8.2) treats income taxed in country A, moved to country B that levies no tax and remitted from B as NOT meeting the condition, and counts 'underlying tax' only as tax on the income out of which the dividend is paid by the paying company. So a dividend paid by a Hong Kong holding company out of Mainland dividends that Hong Kong does not tax fails the condition even though China withheld tax; the rule reads payer_income_taxed / payer_tax_rate of the immediate payer. The optimization layer derives these two facts from the previous hop on this basis.
quote: Country B does not levy any income tax on the income. • The income is remitted back to Singapore from country B. Condition is not met because no tax is suffered in country B.
